name: crewdson-terrace-blue-hour
prompt: Vertical photograph, lens at waist height from the kerb of a narrow British terraced road at dusk, tilted gently upward. Brick terraces line both sides and recede to a vanishing point: front steps, bay windows, satellite dishes, recycling boxes, wheelie bins with yellow and blue lids by every gate, a silver hatchback and a white van parked half on the pavement. Standing in the carriageway, as tall as the rooftops and wider than the road, rises a towering column of loose office paper, sheets fanned slightly at the corners, the top sheet's edge printed in heavy black capitals: THE RULES. Down in the lowest third, tiny beside it, a ragged row of six masked figures tilt their heads back to stare up at it, most seen from behind, two in three-quarter view facing us. Today's streetwear: a quilted gilet, a zipped hoodie, a hi-vis work jacket over a sweatshirt, a long padded coat, tracksuit bottoms, chunky trainers. Each head is hidden under a knitted balaclava in its own colour (mustard, teal, plum, slate, rust, black), solid wool with no eyeholes and no mouth slit, a wide white hoop sewn in a circle across the front, plus one red triangle with softened corners sitting in the hoop's upper right as we look at it, roughly at two o'clock, above the left eye of the person under the mask, never in the middle. Mask hems disappear into upturned collars, hands in black gloves with jacket cuffs reaching down to the knuckles, not a centimetre of skin, cloth only, nothing mechanical. The lighting is theatrical and every source is placed: lamp posts throw pools of orange onto damp tarmac, living-room windows glow honey-yellow behind drawn curtains, a porch light, a television's flicker, and a single hard cold white spotlight from low on one side climbs the paper tower's front so each sheet edge and the printed words stand out crisply. Overhead a clear deep cobalt sky; below it everything warm amber, the two colours meeting at the roofline. Nobody else about, a faint mist, frozen and eerie, a moment held just before something happens. Everything sharp from the figures up to the tower's summit, realistic photograph, fine film grain, the only lettering anywhere is THE RULES.
